ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: It is known that the point $(-3,-1)$ and the point $(4,-6)$ are on two sides of the line $3 x-2 y-a=0$, then the range of values of $a$ is ( )
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Read from the problem stem the two points P=(-3,-1), Q=(4,-6), and the line equation is 3x-2y-a=0. Let F(x,y)=3x-2y-a. Substituting point P gives F(P)=3×(-3)-2×(-1)-a=-9+2-a=-7-a. Substituting point Q gives F(Q)=3×4-2×(-6)-a=12+12-a=24-a. The two points are on opposite sides of the line, equivalent to F(P) and F(Q) having opposite signs, therefore (-7-a)(24-a)<0. Since -7-a=-(a+7), 24-a=-(a-24), the product is equivalent to (a+7)(a-24)<0. Solving gives -7<a<24. Therefore the range of values of a is (-7,24).
